SMTO-UI-0041 — SMTO doesn't recognize these permission settings

GUID: a08492ed-5720-4d8e-aa47-3168953f0ecf
Slug: ui-permission-policy-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Your permission settings decide what the Agent may do without asking you. These settings contain an option this version of SMTO doesn't understand, so it didn't use or save them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page (press Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac). If SMTO was updated while this page was open, the page may be reading the settings in an outdated way.
  2. Select Permissions below the message box. In the Permissions list, choose the option you normally use (Ask is the safest), then select Apply. Choosing one of the listed options replaces the setting SMTO couldn't read with one it understands.
  3. To go back to the usual setup instead, select Use inherited permissions in the same window. When Apply to is Global, this button says Reset to product default. This removes the unreadable setting for that scope and uses the next level's settings.

What success looks like

  • The Permissions window opens and applies without an error, and the permission summary shows the choice you picked.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch to Allow just to make the message go away; that lets the Agent act without asking you.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Permission-policy validation rejected the policy because it is not an object, has an unknown top-level field, a schema_version other than 1, or an unsupported mode or default_confirmation_decision.

What this means

  • Policy canonicalization rejects a non-object, unknown top-level field, unsupported schema version, mode or fallback decision. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Policy canonicalization rejects a non-object, unknown top-level field, unsupported schema version, mode or fallback decision.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare policy shape, version and choices with the supported permission editor.

How to fix it

  • permission_policy.js canonical() throws ui_permission_policy_invalid (and AgentPermissionPolicy.exact_version / extra="forbid" reject it server-side) for non-object values, unknown keys, schema_version != 1, mode outside manual/custom/full_access/deny, or a default decision outside allow/ask/deny. Hard-reload so the browser matches the server build; if a stored scope is malformed, replace it with a supported preset or reset it via the Permissions dialog rather than disabling permission checks.
  • Use the permission editor’s advertised modes and decisions. Keep runtime authorization checks enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The deliberate policy validates under the current schema without weakening runtime authority.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
